question: Should OpenClaw expose a supported global and per-agent opt-in that permits symlinked working directories for approval-bound `system.run` commands while executing from the canonical target?
rationale: The patch is not merely a bug repair: it creates a durable configuration contract that relaxes a deliberately security-hardened path, so code review cannot decide the intended product trust policy alone.

options.title: Approve the opt-in boundary
options.body: Accept the setting if the documented approval UI shows both paths and the canonical target remains revalidated immediately before execution.

options.title: Keep strict canonical cwd policy
options.body: Reject the new setting and retain the existing symlink rejection as the only supported approval-bound execution policy.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the setting if the documented approval UI shows both paths and the canonical target remains revalidated immediately before execution.

likelyOwner.reason: The related canonical report identifies tdjackey with the original TOCTOU hardening whose security invariant this proposal modifies.
